svg.text: Client sends a send_message event (chat id, content, media id) over its persistent WebSocket

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Gateway acts as load balancer plus auth, rate limiting, TLS

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Chat server validates, assigns a globally unique message id and timestamp, and publishes keyed by chat id

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Per-chat partition guarantees order; Kafka also buffers if consumers fail

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Change data capture on the message table triggers the fan-out jobs, so the chat server is not the bottleneck

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Fan-out resolves members of the chat and their active sessions

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Online users: publish to the chat channel (not broadcast to all servers)

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Only WebSocket servers holding a member's connection receive the event

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Server pushes new_message down the socket; the same applies to message_deleted, typing, read receipts, presence

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Offline users get an inbox row instead of a live push

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: A push notification (not the message) tells them to come back

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: On reconnect, pending inbox rows are pushed (skipping deleted ones) and delivered_at is stamped

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Media bytes never pass through the chat server: client uploads to S3 via a pre-signed URL from the media server, then sends only the media id

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • Scale: 1B users (daily active), ~100k concurrent chats, ~12k QPS; latency target 200 ms (batch beyond 500 ms); CAP: availability > consistency

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • Entities: user, chat, chat_member, message (id, chat id, sender, content, parent id), media, device_session. Polyglot persistence: S3 for media, NoSQL for messages

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • Deep dives: ordering (Kafka by chat id), WebSocket scale (Redis pub/sub), WebSocket churn (TTL leases ~10 s), storage (partition + read replicas + cache of members/sessions)
